Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To move the pilot forward our infra team needs two things from Redwood: an estimate of steady-state tokens/sec we'd expect for our usage profile, and a recommended buffer for short peaks (we typically see microbursts during user onboarding flows).

I attached a 3-day request trace (valence_usage_sample.csv) and a quick spreadsheet with named endpoints. We expect to use a 13B-ish completion model for most user routing (approx 350 tokens per request median, 1.2k p95), and we plan to front it with a small Chimera retrieval step that increases request variance.

Can you confirm whether the Dedicated entitlements you mentioned will map directly to tokens/sec, and what headroom you recommend for a pilot commit of ~120k tokens/min? Also interested in guidance for p95 tail latency given quantized variants.

Best,

Hi Ariel —

Thanks for the sample trace. Looping in Ben and Rishi to translate this into tokens/sec and a recommended entitlement layout. Quick answers up front: yes, Dedicated capacity maps to a practical tokens/sec entitlement (we translate GPU slab capacity + model efficiency -> tokens/sec), and pilot commits are often sized with a 1.5–2x peak buffer depending on SLA. We should avoid assuming linear scaling for p95 when batchers and KV caches are in play.

Ben / Rishi — Ariel's team expects ~120k tokens/min sustained (2k tokens/sec) with p95 request sizes much higher. They will use a larger model family for completions; the CSV has per-tenant traffic spikes. Can you produce a scoped estimate (tokens/sec baseline, p95 latency fit for 99/1/0.5 slabs) and a short note on fallbacks (quantized 8-bit vs float16) we should propose?

Kimberly / team / Ariel —

Quick sketch based on the sample:
- Observed median tokens/request: ~340, p95 ~1.15k (matches Ariel's note).
- Sustained baseline of 2k tokens/sec ~= 120k tokens/min. Accounting for batching and cache benefits we estimate an effective GPU throughput requirement equivalent to ~1.6–1.9k tokens/sec of raw model throughput for their workload on an optimized T4-like slab after quantization.

Headroom recommendation (pilot, reserved):
- Baseline entitlement: 2k tokens/sec (to match commit).
- Operational buffer: +50% (spares to absorb onboarding microbursts) => 3k tokens/sec commitment equivalent. This maps to our "Medium Dedicated Slab" (3 units) for the chosen model family.
- Surge policy: allow short bursts up to 6k tokens/sec for 30s via on-demand burst capacity; we recommend configuring autoscaling cooldowns and a throttling circuit at the API layer to preserve p95 objectives.

Latency implications / p95:
- For quantized 8-bit runtime we expect median latency to be within target (<= 180ms), but p95 will stretch if batch windows enlarge under burst. Projected p95 under the Medium slab + 50% buffer: ~260–320ms (model-dependent). Using float16 / faster SKUs reduces p95 by ~60–90ms but increases cost.

Fallback strategy:
- Primary: quantized variant (q4/q8) for cost efficiency.
- Canary: float16 variant for tail-sensitive routes (auth flows, checkout). Use routing by route tag with automatic fallback if p95 > 350ms.

I'll attach a simple entitlement matrix with tokens/sec mapping and SKU assumptions.

—Ben
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Ariel / Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks — I validated the numbers against our runtime benchmarks for the 13B completion path (we used a benchmark model variant similar to their target). A couple of operational clarifications to make this useful for procurement and SRE:

1) Tokens/sec mapping: our entitlement sheet maps 1 "Medium Dedicated Slab" -> ~1k effective tokens/sec for the quantized 13B path (this includes batching and expected KV cache hits). To achieve the recommended 3k tokens/sec you'd request 3 slabs.

2) Cold starts and cache warmup: first-hour onboarding spikes can be 20–40% above trace peaks due to cold KV caches. Recommend a transient credit allowance or a brief warmup window where we temporarily allow 2x burst.

3) SLO profile: If Valence needs an SLA of p95 < 300ms, we recommend 3 slabs + selective float16 routing for <10% of critical traffic. For a looser p95 <= 350ms, 3 slabs with the quantized default and a 50% buffer should suffice.

4) Pricing/ops note: pilot commit of 120k tokens/min with a 50% margin maps to a 3-month pilot minimum of X units (will put numbers in HubSpot deal). We'll also include a burst allowance line item for the first 30 days.

Next steps: Kimberly — want me to prepare a short one-pager that maps slabs->tokens/sec->expected p95 and an ops clause for warmup credits? Ariel, if you can confirm the percentage of traffic that must stay within strict p95 (e.g., auth/checkout), we'll mark those routes for float16 canarying.

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
